sections.markdown:
## C — Point values, the Driver Safety Program, minimum liability insurance, proof of financial responsibility, SR22 rules, reinstatement fees, suspensions, impaired-driving penalties and habitual traffic violators
Knowledge domain: how Indiana scores traffic violations on a driver record, how a defensive driving course earns a point credit, what liability insurance every driver must carry and how to prove it, how SR22 filings and reinstatement fees work, what leads to a suspension, the penalties tied to chemical tests, and when repeated offenses make someone a habitual traffic violator.

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Indiana's Point Study Committee gives each traffic violation a point value that reflects how severe the violation is and its history. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
Driving 1 to 15 miles per hour above the speed limit is an example of a 2-point speeding violation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Driving 16 to 25 miles per hour above the speed limit is listed as a 4-point speeding violation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
Driving 26 or more miles per hour above the speed limit is listed as a 6-point speeding violation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
Not using headlights and driving without brake or signal lights are each listed at 2 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
A hand-held device violation, an unsafe lane movement and ignoring a stop or yield sign are each listed at 4 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A01
Failing to yield to an emergency vehicle and tailgating another vehicle are each listed at 6 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A01
Driving while suspended and taking part in a speed contest on the road are each listed at 8 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A01
Points remain active on an Indiana driver record for two years counted from the date of conviction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A01
Any Indiana driver who finishes a Driver Safety Program course from a BMV-approved provider earns a 4-point credit, but only one such credit is allowed in any 3-year period. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A01
A driver whom the BMV requires to take a Driver Safety Program receives a mailed notice and must complete an approved course within 90 days of the notice date. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A01
The BMV may require a driver aged 21 or older who is convicted of two or more traffic offenses within 12 months to complete an approved Driver Safety Program course. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A01
Missing the 90-day Driver Safety Program deadline suspends driving privileges until the course is completed and the BMV has processed the completion. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A02
When a court orders a Driver Safety Program, the court chooses the type, but the 4-point credit is applied only for a BMV-approved course. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A02
The BMV needs about 7 to 10 business days to process Driver Safety Program completion results. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A02
Indiana law bars anyone from driving a motor vehicle in the state unless financial responsibility (insurance) is in effect for that vehicle or the driver is otherwise insured. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A02
Indiana's minimum liability coverage, known as 25/50/25, is $25,000 for injury or death of one person, $50,000 for injury or death of two or more people in one accident, and $25,000 for property damage in one accident. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A02
If the BMV asks for proof of insurance, contact your insurer right away and have it send a Certificate of Compliance (COC) to the BMV electronically. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A02
Situations that can trigger a BMV request to verify insurance include an auto accident, a serious violation such as a misdemeanor or felony, and a pointable moving violation within one year of two other pointable moving violations. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A02
The insurer's Certificate of Compliance must reach and be processed by the BMV within 90 days of the BMV mailing its request, or driving privileges are suspended. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A02
A suspension from a court conviction for driving uninsured, or for not filing insurance with the BMV, is lifted only after the insurer electronically files an SR22 showing future financial responsibility. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A03
An SR22 shows that a policy meets the state minimums, and the policy cannot be canceled unless the BMV is notified first. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A03
A no-insurance suspension that took effect on or after 12/31/2021 is indefinite; an SR22 stays it, and keeping the SR22 continuously for 180 days ends it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A03
If the insurer sends the BMV an SR26 cancellation notice while an SR22 is required, the BMV suspends driving privileges until a new SR22 is on file or the requirement period ends. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A03
For no-insurance suspensions after Jan. 1, 2015, reinstatement fees are $250 for the first, $500 for the second, and $1,000 for the third or any later suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A03
A driver can skip the no-insurance reinstatement fee by having the insurer file an SR22 electronically and keeping it in force without a break for 180 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A03
Not appearing in court on a citation, or not paying a ticket after judgment, can lead to a suspension that the court tells the BMV to close once you appear or pay. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A03
Driving while suspended is a serious violation, and doing it with a prior offense can produce a misdemeanor or felony conviction on the record. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A03
Driving while intoxicated, or with a blood alcohol concentration above the legal limit of .08, is a criminal offense. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A03
The main factors that set a person's BAC are how much alcohol was drunk, how fast it was drunk and the person's body weight. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A04
A driver who fails a chemical test faces a 180-day suspension, refusing the test brings a 1-year suspension, and refusing with a prior intoxicated-driving conviction brings a 2-year suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A04
After an intoxicated-driving conviction a court may require an ignition interlock device, which checks the driver's blood alcohol before the car will start. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A04
An intoxicated-watercraft conviction is sent to the BMV, goes on the driver record and carries the same driving-privilege penalties as one in a motor vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A04
Paying the BMV with funds that are not honored leads to an indefinite suspension until the amount owed plus service, collection and reinstatement fees is paid. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F35 | anchor: A04
Your driver record can be viewed free at any time on myBMV.com once you set up an account. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F36 | anchor: A05
A person who, within 10 years, collects two judgments for offenses causing injury or death, such as reckless homicide or failing to stop after an injury crash, becomes a habitual traffic violator with a 10-year suspension. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F37 | anchor: A06
A driver with 10 or more traffic violations in 10 years, at least one of them a major offense, is a habitual traffic violator under Section C and faces a 5-year suspension. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F38 | anchor: A06
A court-granted hardship, probationary, conditional or specialized driving privilege places Restriction 5 on the person's license. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0031]

Misconceptions: points do not disappear the moment a ticket is paid, they stay active for two years from conviction; a court-ordered course earns the point credit only when it is BMV-approved; refusing a chemical test brings a longer suspension than failing one; paying a reinstatement fee is not the only way back, a continuous SR22 can replace it.
Mnemonics: twenty-five, fifty, twenty-five for the insurance minimums; ninety days for both the safety course notice and the insurance proof request; two, four, six for the speeding bands; fail one-eighty days, refuse one year, refuse again two years.
Glossary: COC means Certificate of Compliance, the insurer's electronic proof of coverage; SR22 means the insurer's filing of future financial responsibility; SR26 means the insurer's notice cancelling an SR22; DSP means Driver Safety Program, a BMV-approved defensive driving course; HTV means habitual traffic violator; BAC means blood alcohol concentration.
Dynamic facts: reinstatement fee amounts, the official record price, the BMV phone line, State Form numbers, the approved course provider list and myBMV.com services can change; confirm them on IN.gov/BMV.

corpus_stability.reason: The Indiana Driver's Manual back cover reads Published July 2026 and tells readers to check IN.gov/BMV for updates; the BMV manual page says printed manuals are updated at most once a year, so the selected pages are treated as stable within a year while fees and service details stay dynamic.
